title: Adversarial prefix-preservation eval + hit-aware scoring for KV/prefix cache regressions
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: We continue to see subtle semantic shifts when requests hit the KV/prefix cache. Existing delta-evals focus on Golden response diffs or hit/non-hit overall deltas, but they miss adversarial examples and structured prompt transformations that reveal semantic flips only on cache hits. Goal: build an adversarial, hit-conditioned eval harness and a hit-aware scoring metric that surfaces semantic regressions caused specifically by prefix cache reuse, including low-frequency and edge-case prompts. Outputs should integrate into Console alerts and canary gates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible harness (hit-fuzzer) that can 1) force simulated cache-hits and 2) fuzz prefix KV entries to produce adversarial variations; 2) New hit-aware scoring function (HitDeltaScore) that reports per-prompt semantic regression risk and aggregates by model/config; 3) A baseline run across existing prompt suites showing prioritized regression candidates; 4) Runbook and canary gating rule (auto-block rollout when aggregated HitDeltaScore > threshold) documented and reviewed.
approach:
- Generate adversarial variants from seed prompts via structured transformations (trailing punctuation, casing swaps, whitespace injection, ellipsis expansion, canonicalization removals) and semantic paraphrases (back-translation + paraphrase model).
- Produce hit-conditioned pairs: (no-cache-run, forced-cache-hit-run) by instrumenting the runtime to return responses under both paths for identical requests.
- Measure semantic delta using ensemble metrics (BERTScore, MoverScore, cosine(Embedding), and a new hit-penalty term that weights differences at the top-k token-level probability mass).
- Rank prompts by HitDeltaScore (combination of semantic drop and downstream metric impact like intent classification mismatch).
- Implement a fuzz-mode that mutates stored KV cache values to emulate stale/partial-prefix writes and observe model output sensitivity.
- Surface top candidates to engineers with minimial reproduction artifacts: request payload, model + weights hash, KV key + simulated prefix, and deterministic seed.
tradeoffs:
- Running forced no-cache vs forced-cache doubles compute for the eval suite; mitigated by stratified sampling and early stopping on low-risk prompts.
- Adversarial transforms may produce unrealistic prompts; to counter, we keep a human-review tier and rely on paraphrase probabilities to weight plausibility.
- Hit-aware scoring increases complexity of dashboards and alerting; we will add it as an opt-in alert for two weeks before making it default.
instrumentation_changes:
- Add /internal/eval/force_cache_hint flag to runtime and a testmode that can inject mutated KV entries.
- Add telemetry: hit_condition (forced|observed|none), kv_simulation_hash, transform_id, bert_delta, embedding_cosine_delta.
- New SLO for eval accuracy of HitDeltaScore vs human label (target 0.85 agreement on top 200 flagged prompts).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement harness + local runs on small prompt set (1 week). Phase 2: run full suite on staging models, collect baselines (2 weeks). Phase 3: enable canary alerts in Console for runtime-1.20 deployments (1 week). Phase 4: integrate into auto-rollout gates with fallback to no-cache variant when HitDeltaScore exceeds threshold (post-review).
runbook:
- When an alert fires: 1) check hit_condition and transform_id in payload; 2) reproduce with forced no-cache and forced-cache to confirm delta; 3) inspect KV contents and recent write history; 4) if regression confirmed, rollback to no-cache fallback for the impacted traffic slice and open a debug PR referencing this ticket.
- Escalation: page runtime on-call if customer-facing SLA is affected.
notes_and_feedback: 2025-02-13: Initial design review with PM + Research. Agreed to prioritize seed prompts from customer-facing eval sets and internal PLG flows.
2025-02-20: Design feedback from Design: include a visualization of token-level divergence and an example overlay in Console to explain semantic flips to non-ML owners.
2025-02-25: Engineering sync: Luca to prototype forced-cache flag and fuzz-kv in a sandbox cluster. Asha will prepare baseline prompt cluster definitions.

2025-03-03: Early prototype results: out of 2k prompts, 42 flagged high-risk by HitDeltaScore. Manual review found 11 clear semantic flips affecting entity extraction. Decided to tighten paraphrase plausibility threshold to reduce false positives.
